name: Instagram tan filter / photo editing

lead: Some people use filters, editing apps or lighting to make their skin look darker or warmer in photos.
Nothing specific to tan filters has been studied.

paras: Software adjusts colour and tone in an image; no change to actual skin occurs.
Research on beauty filters generally reports a correlation with negative body image, with unclear causation.[1]

lead: Editing or lighting photos to look tanner is a form of digital appearance enhancement in which colour grading, filters or retouching apps darken or warm skin tone in images. It sits within the broader category of social media beauty filters, which smooth skin, reshape features and apply virtual makeup.[1]
The sources reviewed do not discuss tan-specific filters. Research on filters in general links their use to body-image concerns, though the direction of causation is unknown.[1]

paras: Beauty filters trace back to Japanese Purikura photo booths of 1995 and became widespread on Instagram and Snapchat in the 2010s.[1] Common effects listed include skin smoothing, virtual makeup and slimming or reshaping the face.[1]

Critics and researchers have raised concerns about unrealistic beauty standards, and terms such as "filter dysmorphia" describe insecurity from comparing oneself with filtered images. A correlation between filter use and negative body image has been reported, with causation unestablished.[1]
